slots.description: The form's business slots, in prompt priority order. Each is a slot the app's code defines.

summaryPromptId.description: The prompt (an id in prompts.yaml) that reads the filled form back for a yes, or null for a form with no summary (it completes as soon as its slots are full).

hooks.description: The code hooks this form uses, written in the app's TypeScript; "complete" is required, unless the form `answers` from the knowledge base (its completion is then the engine's) or goes on to a `next` form (its completion is then that form). entry (the call made before the slots are asked), onEntry (applies its result), principalEntry (in its place for someone acting for subjects), confirmedParams (the values a confirmed write sends, for the gate's confirmed rule), complete (runs when the form is full and confirmed), onAnswers (hears every spoken turn), onSummaryAnswer (moves along what the summary offers), keepsSlot (keeps a slot the caller named when changing), onSummaryRead (looks at what the summary is about to name).

answers.description: The form says an answer from the knowledge base, and its completion is the engine's: the answer resolved through the gate for the topic in `slot`, said word for word with the topic's account line where it has one (or, where the answer line frames its {answer} as a span `from: answer` and the topic is `risk: low`, the approved passage worded for the caller's question, the account line after it), or the unavailable line and a person offered, once per call. A form with `answers` has no "complete" hook.

slot.description: The form's topic slot: its value is the topic the caller asked about.

via.description: The gated action that resolves the answer (a tool in the code, with an action in policy.yaml, returning an answer or why there is none). Default: kb/kb.yaml's action.

answer.description: The prompt the answer is said through; its text says {answer}. Default: kb_answer.

unavailable.description: The prompt said when there is no answer to give, before a person is offered. Default: kb_unavailable.

subject.description: A slot of this form that names the subject the answer is about, for a caller who is not one of the app's subjects (a delegate acting for them, asked it with the slot's askedOf): its value goes to the resolving action and an account line's tool as the subject param, and the gate's scope rule decides whether this caller may read that subject's answer. A subject is always answered about themselves. Default: none, and a caller who is not a subject is answered about no one (the scope rule refuses).

midTask.description: What asking for this form while another is open does to that form. aside (the default): the form in hand is set aside as it stands, the answer is said, and the form resumes where it was (its question, or its summary or confirmation asked again), whether the caller replaced the task with the question or added it; the topic said with the question is the one answered (the topic is asked in a second, small request on the same words). With no answer to give, the unavailable line is said and a person offered, once per call, as for an informational intent's passage; turned down, the form resumes. task: the form is a task like any other, as before this option: it replaces the form in hand or is queued after it, as the model reads the turn, and its topic is asked once it is open.

calls.description: The actions (tools) this form's hooks call through the gate: its entry call and the calls its completion makes. Declare it for every form or for none (an empty list for a form that calls nothing): the app map draws each form to its actions, and `check` reports an action that no form reaches and the identity flow does not call. A check action is reached through `checks`, not listed here.

checks.description: Actions the gate decides on part-way through the form, in the order written: each runs as soon as the slots it reads are filled (after the entry call, before the next question, and again at completion), and again whenever one of them changes. ALLOW lets the form go on; a refusal ends the form with the line and the ending `on` maps its reason to. Checks ask the model nothing.

action.description: The action the gate decides on: an action in policy.yaml with check: true (no tool runs; the gate only answers).

with.description: The form's slots the check reads, each sent as the param of the same name. The check runs once every one of them holds a value, and again whenever one of them changes. An identity factor may be named too (check warns): it holds a value only once the caller has given it during verification.

on.description: A refusal reason (the gate's reason) mapped to its line and how the form ends. A reason not listed gets the engine's refusal: a BLOCK with a line from the app's blockPromptId says it and the call carries on; anything else goes to a person. A STEP_UP asks for identity, as an entry call's does, and the check runs again once the caller is verified (in an app without identity.yaml, it goes to a person).

confirm.description: A yes-or-no line (a prompt in prompts.yaml) said before the refusal acts, when a slot the check reads has not been confirmed; it renders with the form's slot displays as variables, as `say` does. A yes confirms them and the refusal acts; a no empties them and asks again, and the check runs again when they fill. Skipped when every slot it reads is confirmed already (a read-back, or the summary's yes). Default: none, the refusal acts at once.

say.description: The line said (a prompt in prompts.yaml); it renders with the form's slot displays as variables, as the summary does. Required for end and anything-else; for the others, said first.

then.description: What follows the line: end (the call ends after the line; with a request queued, the call goes on to it); anything-else (the form closes uncompleted and the call carries on: the next queued request, or "anything else?"); handoff (to a person, with the handoff line handoff_<reason>); form (the form closes uncompleted and the form named by `form` is entered, as a next: is, keeping the slots both list).

reason.description: For then: handoff, the handoff reason, whose line is handoff_<reason>. Default: the reason the gate gave.

form.description: For then: form, the form entered: a form in forms.yaml (an internal one too).

goodbye.description: For then: end, whether the app's goodbye line follows `say`. false: the call ends on `say` alone, for a line that says goodbye itself ("... We're closed right now. Goodbye."), so the caller does not hear goodbye twice. Default true: the goodbye follows the line. Either way, with a request queued the line is said and the call goes on to it, so a line that may be followed by one keeps the goodbye out of its words (only a start route never has one).

additionalProperties.description: What a refusal for this reason does: a line, and how the form ends.

items.description: One check: an action the gate decides on as soon as the slots it reads are filled.

checksPassed.description: A line said once, on the turn every check of the form has passed (never again after a correction). It renders with the form's slot displays as variables. Only with checks.

next.description: The form entered at once when this one completes (its complete hook answers `said`, or it has none, which `next` allows): the slots both forms list are kept, with their values and confirmations, and the next form is bridged into (bridge_next with its label), ahead of any request the caller queued. A completion that ends the call, a refusal, or a check that ends the form does not go on. Usually an internal form (a booking after a screen); it may be a form intent too.

internal.description: true: the form is not an intent. The model, the keypad menu and the queue never see it; it is reached only by another form's `next`, and it has no intent in intents.yaml. Needs a `label`. Default false.

label.description: An internal form's spoken label ("book your free inspection"), as an intent's label is used: in bridge_next as {intentLabel}, and as the form the caller is in. Only on an internal form; a form intent's label is in intents.yaml.

summary.description: How the form's summary answers a caller who pushes back. Only on a form with a summary.

onNo.description: What a bare no at the summary does (a no that changes nothing). ask-change (the default): "What should I change?" (ask_change), as always. read-back: the summary is read again word for word first, after read_back_exact (a line the app writes), never generated whatever its when says, and with no attempt counted; a second bare no goes on to ask_change, and the ladder continues as always. With read-back, asking to hear it again at ask_change reads the summary again, word for word.

wording.description: How the form's lines are produced (generated wording). generative: each of its lines (its slots' questions, ask_<slot> and their retry, no-input and partial lines, their read-backs, confirm_<slot>, and its summary) is generated as a prompt with mode: generative is, unless the line says mode: fixed or is prescribed (prescribed: true). A line without a goal of its own is worded to say what its fixed text says. Default fixed: every line word for word.

acknowledge.description: With wording: generative: whether the lines its switch generates may begin by acknowledging what the caller just said. false: each only rewords its fixed line. Default true; a line's own `acknowledge` in prompts.yaml wins.

listenBeforeEntered.description: Whether the form's slots fill from what the caller says before the form is open (on the turn that opens it, as `listen: up-front` does). false: a slot every form that lists it says false for behaves as `listen: form`, and is asked once its form is open, even when it was said earlier. A slot's own `listen` overrides it. Default true for a form intent, false for an internal form.

additionalProperties.description: One form: the slots it collects, the summary it reads back, the code hooks it uses (or the knowledge answer it says), and the actions it calls.

forms.description: Every form, by id. Each id must also be a form intent in intents.yaml, unless the form is internal (reached only by another form's next).

description: forms.yaml: the forms the app runs.
